Investigating a springA spring obeys F = ke up to 6.0 N. Its extension at 6.0 N is 0.030 m. Use E = 0.5ke². Design an investigation to determine the spring constant and identify the limit of proportionality. Include measurements, processing and safety.
scheme: 1 · Clamp spring securely next to a vertical ruler and measure unloaded length.
2 · Add known weights in small increments and allow spring to settle.
3 · Measure loaded length at eye level and calculate extension by subtraction.
4 · Repeat readings/unload to check reproducibility and whether original length is recovered.
5 · Plot force against extension; gradient of initial straight-line region gives k and departure marks limit of proportionality.
6 · Secure stand/use eye protection and prevent masses falling on feet; avoid excessive loads. Safety must be included for full 6 marks.
